target_mass.quote: eight LiF bolometers with a total mass of 168g

summary.plain: A University of Tokyo experiment in the Kamioka mine, Japan, that used small fluoride crystals (lithium fluoride, then sodium fluoride) cooled to near absolute zero to look for dark matter particles that interact through nuclear spin, and set limits on their couplings.
summary.technical: Arrays of eight LiF (168 g) or NaF (176 g) bolometers with NTD-Ge thermistors in a dilution refrigerator below 10 mK, 2700 m.w.e., in a laboratory excavated near Super-Kamiokande (Mozumi mine). Spin-dependent WIMP searches: 4.1 kg d of LiF (2001-2002) and 3.38 kg d of NaF (2002-2003) give limits in the a_p-a_n plane, excluding much of the UKDMC-allowed region.

technology.quote: The detector used in this dark matter search experiment is a LiF bolometer array consisting of eight LiF bolometers with a total mass of 168g.
technology.value: Arrays of eight LiF or NaF crystal bolometers with NTD germanium thermistors, read out below 10 mK in a dilution refrigerator
